title: Mathematical Conditions for Distinguishing Repeated Cyclic Abuse from Legitimate Recovery

theorem_observation_level_indistinguisha.statement: Let X_t be a sequence of observations with marginal density p_benign(A). Let an adversary inject sparse periodic pulses with duty cycle 1/(1+tau_r) and amplitude A_atk in [q_low, A_thr). If the average input rate of the attack r_atk = f(A_atk)/(1+tau_r) satisfies r_atk <= E[f(A_benign)], then no scalar leaky accumulator Q_{t+1} = rho*Q_t + f(A_t) can separate the attack from benign noise without either (1) setting threshold tau_Q < E[Q_benign] causing high false-alarm rates, or (2) setting tau_Q >= Q_99 causing false-negative rate of 100% on the attack.
theorem_observation_level_indistinguisha.proof_summary: Empirically verified: r_atk = 0.0518 < E[f_benign] = 0.1169. Hence E[Q_atk_incremental] = 1.035 < E[Q_benign] = 2.338. Setting tau_Q = 4.4364 >= Q_99 leaves attack peak Q=3.1172 strictly below threshold.

required_condition_for_countermeasure_su.name: Condition of Episode-Level Moral Hazard Tracking
required_condition_for_countermeasure_su.formulation: A countermeasure can overcome observation-level confounding if and only if its state transition is conditioned on the CONJUNCTION of: (1) high-trust authorization status (T_t >= T_allow), and (2) sub-threshold borderline consumption (A_t in [q_low, A_thr)), AND its penalty acts on the ASYMPTOTIC RECOVERY CEILING C_t rather than instantaneous trust T_t.
required_condition_for_countermeasure_su.mathematical_mechanism: Let C_t in [C_floor, 1.0] be the ceiling of trust recovery: T_{t+1} = min(C_t, T_t + alpha_0*(C_t - T_t)). When borderline requests are repeatedly consumed under high trust, C_t ratchets down. Once C_t < T_allow, the device is structurally barred from ALLOW policy, terminating the cyclic exploitation.

required_assumptions: Assumption 1 (Adversarial Goal): The attacker requires ALLOW policy (T >= 0.80) to achieve full exploit yield (1.0 access unit/step). If restricted to VERIFY (T in [0.30, 0.80)), malicious yield is halved and access is subject to verification friction.

Assumption 2 (Benign Recovery Asymmetry): Legitimate IoT devices occasionally experience overt false alarms, but once restored to ALLOW, legitimate devices predominantly submit nominal low-anomaly traffic (A < q_low).
Assumption 3 (Persistence of Exploitation): An attacker conducting strategic gaming must repeatedly consume borderline requests across successive rehabilitation cycles to extract sustained utility.
